site.frontage: A360 High Street, to the south-west
site.note: Lat/lon derived from the MAGiC grid reference via OSGB36->WGS84 Helmert transform. Accurate to ~1m; good enough for a true sun path.
site.orientationNote: The agent plan is drawn with 'up' pointing approximately north-east, not north. That makes the kitchen/dining wing north-west, the dining and living rooms south-west (facing the A360), the living room south-east and the garage north-east. Confirmed by the architect's elevation names (NW / SE / SW) and by the plot's alignment to the road on the title plan. All room coordinates below stay in plan space; planRotationDeg rotates the model to true north for the sun path.

assumptions.title: Garage may be detached rather than attached
assumptions.detail: The aerial shows the garage as its own hipped brick block with two up-and-over doors, reading as newer than the house. Whether it truly abuts the living-room wall or is linked by a short connection changes the envelope. Modelled as abutting.

assumptions.title: Attached structure has no known dimensions
assumptions.detail: The architect's 1:50 plan shows it clearly but the scan carries no legible figures or scale bar. Footprint modelled as a 7.0 x 4.8m estimate from proportions. A PDF of the same sheet, or two real dimensions, replaces this.

assumptions.title: Is the attached structure inside the title?
assumptions.detail: The title plan shows a separately outlined building to the south-west labelled 79a. Whether the attached structure is part of 79, part of 79a, or a third element determines whether it belongs in this model at all.

assumptions.title: First floor is deeper than the ground floor
assumptions.detail: The plan labels the north-west bedroom 4.07m deep. Stacked on the 3.64m bedroom below it that needs 7.81m of internal depth, but the ground floor (kitchen 3.02 + dining 3.64) only gives 6.76m. Modelled here as the west wing projecting ~1.0m north of the ground floor. The stepped outline on the title plan supports this. NEEDS CONFIRMING.

assumptions.title: Which wall is the party wall?
assumptions.detail: Records describe the property as semi-detached. The attached single-storey structure at the kitchen end is the likely reason for that classification, rather than a two-storey party wall. Modelled as attached at the north-west kitchen wall.

assumptions.title: North-east ground floor layout is simplified
assumptions.detail: The plan shows a bathroom, a separate shower cubicle, a WC and the hall packed into this zone. Modelled as one bathroom plus hall pending room photos.

assumptions.title: Window positions and widths are approximate
assumptions.detail: Read off the plan by proportion. Sill 0.9m, head 2.1m throughout. Elevation photos will fix these.

assumptions.title: No bathroom on the first floor
assumptions.detail: Three bedrooms upstairs and all sanitary ware downstairs. Taken from the plan at face value; unusual enough to be worth confirming.

assumptions.title: Ceiling heights inferred from photographs, not measured
assumptions.detail: 2.65m ground, 2.35m kitchen, 2.45m first floor, read from picture-rail and coving proportions. A tape measure on any one wall corrects all of them.

assumptions.title: One bathroom cannot be placed with confidence
assumptions.detail: A shower room appears with a sloping ceiling and a small high-level window, which means it sits under a roof slope — either upstairs off the landing, or in a single-storey section. The agent plan puts all sanitary ware on the ground floor. Which is it?

assumptions.title: A rendered/panelled structure abuts the rear flank
assumptions.detail: The rear photo shows a large white panelled wall with failing paint hard against the property. Age and material unknown — if it is asbestos cement sheeting that matters well beyond the model.

levels.name: Ground floor
levels.note: Living and dining rooms carry a picture rail and deep coving — reads as 2.6-2.7m.

levels.name: First floor
levels.note: Bedroom photo shows the ceiling sloping in from the hip on one side. The roof geometry supplies that slope.

ceilingSlope.note: Ceilings slope in at the outer corners on all three bedrooms, the landing and the shower room. Generated from the roof geometry rather than declared per room.

rooms.name: Kitchen
rooms.label: 3.64 x 3.02m
rooms.note: Lower ceiling with an angled soffit over the run of units — reads as a later addition rather than original fabric.

openings.note: Plan shows a door at the garage's north-west corner into the hall

stairs.note: Straight flight on the ground floor, winder at the top on the first-floor plan.

roof.source: Aerial photograph — hipped roof on both house and garage, two brick chimneys on the main block.

structures.name: Attached single-storey structure
structures.note: Aerial confirms a pitched clay-tile roof with a half-timbered gable and glazed doors — matching the architect's south-east elevation. Footprint still a proportional estimate.

features.note: Stone-clad surround, wood-burning stove, alcove each side.
Brick fireplace with timber mantel; built-in alcove shelving to one side.
Cast-iron bedroom fireplace with painted timber surround.
Landing is naturally lit by its own window, with a turned-newel staircase and spindle balustrade.

construction.walls: red brick, exposed on the flank and rear; the south-west front is largely covered by Virginia creeper
construction.periodEvidence: Hipped roof, picture rails and deep coving, tall ground-floor ceilings, cast-iron bedroom fireplaces, brick chimney breasts to both floors.
construction.wallThicknessNote: Inter-war brick could be solid 9-inch (230mm) or early cavity (270-300mm). Still using 300mm. An EPC or a reveal measurement at any window settles it.

outbuildings.location: rear patio, against the flank wall
